key_insight: PosteriorBench shifts evaluation of generative inverse solvers from "did it produce a good-looking sample?" to "does it match the full posterior distribution?". This matters because in ill-posed inverse problems, a single accurate reconstruction can still hide mode collapse, overconfidence, or missed solution modes.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the weakness of existing evaluation protocols for generative inverse problems: they mostly measure point-estimate quality and fail to assess whether a model captures the true uncertainty and multi-modality of the posterior.
method: Introduces PosteriorBench, a benchmark focused on posterior matching rather than only reconstruction accuracy.
Evaluates whether generative inverse solvers reproduce the distribution of valid solutions under sparse or noisy observations.
Highlights failure modes such as mode collapse, overconfident uncertainty estimates, and averaging across plausible solutions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a more reliable way to judge inverse solvers in science and engineering settings where uncertainty matters. It encourages building models that are not only accurate, but also calibrated and distributionally faithful.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of point estimate evaluation vs posterior matching evaluation

Pipeline diagram of an inverse problem: observation -> generative solver -> candidate reconstructions
Failure-mode icons for mode collapse, overconfidence, and averaging
paper_title: PosteriorBench: From Point Estimates to Posterior Matching in Evaluating Generative Inverse Solvers
paper_authors: Jiachen Yao, Zi-Siang Hsu, Xi Deng, Aditi Gupta, Xin Ju
